annotation.title_clean: Written contributions on possible consensus recommendations in relation to the clarification, consideration and development of aspects of the normative and operational framework on Emerging Technologies in the Area of Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.title_en: Written contributions on possible consensus recommendations in relation to the clarification, consideration and development of aspects of the normative and operational framework on Emerging Technologies in the Area of Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United Kingdom (submission to CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts (CCW/GGE.1/2021/WP.11)
annotation.summary_en: UK working paper to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts proposing consensus recommendations on lethal autonomous weapons. It argues existing IHL suffices, and urges lifecycle-based good practice, legal weapon reviews, a compendium of best practice, attention to the human role and control, and norms for responsible use.
key_provisions_or_claims: CCW remains the optimum forum for LAWS; existing IHL and weapons regulation can govern new capabilities.
Use the six-phase weapon lifecycle to operationalise the eleven guiding principles.
Focus on the human role and control across the whole lifecycle, not only at the point of use.
Strengthen legal weapon reviews and share a compendium of good practice.
State responsibility and individual accountability cannot be negated by autonomy; develop norms and national policy principles.
